settings.heading: A handcart near the dairy market
settings.body:
In 1919, Gangaprasad Bhai began selling fresh mithai from a handcart in Anand — then a small dairy town in Gujarat, now known the world over as India's “Milk Capital.” His recipes came from his mother's kitchen: real cow's milk, real ghee, nothing stretched or substituted.

A hundred years and three generations later, the recipes haven't changed. What has: we now ship pan-India, same-day-fresh, so the sweets that once only reached one street in Anand can reach your doorstep.

Family portrait — a real shoot is planned before this store's actual launch; the photo above stands in for it.

settings.title: A cart in Anand
settings.body: Gangaprasad Bhai starts selling fresh mithai from a handcart near the dairy market, using recipes passed down from his mother.

settings.title: The first shop
settings.body: The family opens a small storefront on the same street, still using the same brass kadhai for the katli.

settings.title: Third generation
settings.body: Grandsons take over daily operations, adding festival hampers and namkeen while keeping every recipe unchanged.

settings.title: Still handmade, daily
settings.body: Every batch is still made fresh each morning in Anand and shipped pan-India, no preservatives, same family recipes.
